'''Warren G. Abrahamson''' is an American biologist. He is Professor of Biology ''[[Emeritus]]'' at [[Bucknell University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Donnelly |first=Shannon |title=Archbold Biological Station honors Warren Abrahamson, professor emeritus |url=https://www.palmbeachdailynews.com/story/entertainment/society/2014/04/06/archbold-biological-station-honors-warren/9654865007/ |access-date=2025-09-25 |website=Palm Beach Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref> He retired in 2012, having begun at the college as a teacher and researcher in 1973.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Warren G. Abrahamson |url=https://warrengabrahamson.scholar.bucknell.edu/ |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=Bucknell University |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Abrahamson, who was born to Warren and Alice Abrahamson,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Remembering the life of Jill Abrahamson |url=https://obituaries.dailyitem.com/obituary/jill-abrahamson-1017208522 |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=obituaries.dailyitem.com |language=en}}</ref> graduated from the [[University of Michigan]].<ref name=":0" />

In 1972, he was awarded the Lindback Award for Distinguished Teaching. A decade later, he was awarded The Class of 1956 Lectureship Award.<ref name=":0" /> In 1984, he was awarded the [[Audubon|National Audubon Society]]'s [[William Dutcher]] Award for Outstanding Service to the Audubon Cause at the Regional Level (Mid-Atlantic Region).

He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2008.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellow/abrahamson-warren |title=Abrahamson, Warren |publisher=aaas.org |accessdate=April 21, 2017}}</ref>

=== Bucknell Greenhouse ===
Around 1990, Abrahamson helped design the Bucknell Biology Greenhouse during the department's relocation from the Botany Building.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Greenhouse |url=http://www.departments.bucknell.edu/biology/facilities/greenhouse.html |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=www.departments.bucknell.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Green house 1945 |url=https://www.departments.bucknell.edu/edu/bu_history_old/photo_history/1945/interiors/greenhouse.html |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=www.departments.bucknell.edu}}</ref> He created a self-guiding tour for the greenhouse,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Self-Guiding Tour of the Biology Greenhouse |url=http://www.departments.bucknell.edu/biology/facilities/tour.html |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=www.departments.bucknell.edu}}</ref> which is located on the fourth floor of the [[Robert Levi Rooke|Robert L. Rooke]] Science Center.<ref>[https://www.virtually-anywhere.net/tours/bucknell/campus/vtour/index.html?startscene=scene_Rooke_Science_Building Rooke Science Building] – Virtually Anywhere</ref> Julia Knickerbocker was the greenhouse's caretaker at the Botany Building.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Checklist of Plants in Bucknell Greenhouse - Title |url=http://www.departments.bucknell.edu/biology/facilities/plants.html |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=www.departments.bucknell.edu}}</ref> She was succeeded by Dr. Mark Spiro, who is now Associate Professor of Biology and Bucknell Farm's director.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mark Spiro - Associate Professor of Biology; Farm Director |url=https://www.bucknell.edu/fac-staff/mark-spiro |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=www.bucknell.edu |language=en}}</ref> Tasha Hall has held the role since 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tasha Hall - Greenhouse Caretaker |url=https://www.bucknell.edu/fac-staff/tasha-hall |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=www.bucknell.edu |language=en}}</ref>

Upon Abrahamson's retirement in 2012, Dr. Chris Martine succeeded him.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chris Martine - David Burpee Professor in Plant Genetics & Research |url=https://www.bucknell.edu/fac-staff/chris-martine |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=www.bucknell.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Abrahamson is married to Chris, with whom he lives on Shamokin Mountain, near [[Lewisburg, Pennsylvania]].<ref name=":0" /> Their daughter, Jill, died in 2017, aged 44.<ref name=":1" />
